portion_doctrine: Adobe Premiere Pro Masterclass video transcription (segments 91-100). Heavy procedural content on audio dynamics processing, loudness metering, title animation, and editing. Minimal strategic value for SNIPED. This is educational tutorial boilerplate / step-by-step UI guidance, not applicable to founder operating context.
operating_rules: Use multiple compressors (not just one) to handle different frequency ranges: dynamics processor for breath reduction + fast limiter for peak control
Set compressor attack time to 0 ms for fast peak limiting; higher attack times (26ms) create smoother expansion but less compression
Master bus requires: (1) protection layer against inter-sample peak clipping, (2) loudness monitoring
True peak level should never exceed -1 dB to avoid lossy audio format distortion (MP3, AAC)
Integrated loudness targets: YouTube -14 to -15 LUFS, Apple Podcast/Netflix/Spotify vary by platform
Use Loudness Meter effect on master bus as monitoring layer before limiting
ISP (Inter-Sample Peak) limiting with ceiling at -1 to -1.5 dB as final protection stage
Title animation formula: opacity keyframe (fade in/out) + scale keyframe (zoom 100% to 110%) + ease-in on exit
Cross-dissolve transitions work, but manual opacity + scale keyframes produce smoother appearance
Set Cross Dissolve as default transition (Ctrl+D) to speed up applied transitions across timeline
Animate title sequences by: (1) pre-animate one title with full effect chain, (2) duplicate + modify text, (3) offset timing so next title fades in as previous fades out
named_methods: Dynamics Processor expansion technique: set sub-threshold point to pull down in-between silence moments, creating dynamic range expansion
Dual-compressor strategy: slow expander for breath reduction + fast attack limiter for peak blocking
FIRCOMP effect workflow: third-party free compressor for sub-1ms attack without distortion (alternative to native dynamics processor)
Limiter Number 6 mastering plugin: free ISP-precise limiting with peak limiter + leveling compressor sections
Title fade-in/zoom animation sequence: opacity 0%-100%-100%-0% + scale 100%-110% with ease-in applied, duplicated and time-offset
numbers: Attack time 0 ms: hard limiting reaction speed
Attack time 26 ms: smooth expansion without chatter
-20 dB input threshold: dynamics processor compression target
-1 dB true peak ceiling: maximum safe amplitude before inter-sample clipping
-1.5 dB: acceptable ISP ceiling upper bound
-14 to -15 LUFS: YouTube integrated loudness target
110% scale: title zoom end value (10% increase)
4x oversampling mode: helps reduce aliasing in Limiter Number 6
-3 to -5 dB: threshold range for peak limiter settings (content-dependent)
200 USD/year: subscription cost for Universe plugin suite (mentioned as reference)
specific_tactics: Apply dynamics processor in audio track mixer (not on clip itself) for real-time control
Set compression curve to hard-limit above threshold, expansion curve below threshold, in same dynamics processor
Monitor true peak with Loudness Meter before it hits the final limiter stage
If integrated loudness is way low (-20 LUFS), don't rely on platform auto-leveling; manually bring to target before delivery
For multiple-source audio levels: use Essential Sound panel to mark tracks as 'Dialog', run auto-match loudness, then apply conservative S-curve on dynamics processor
Title animation timing: start fade-in 3 bars in, end at full opacity, reverse keyframes at end of clip duration for fade-out
Offset duplicated titles by just a few frames so next title begins fade-in as previous ends fade-out (overlap prevention)
Use color gradation in title text: anchor brand color at endpoint, fade to white at beginning, creating visual progression across sequence
tools: Adobe Premiere Pro: Audio Track Mixer > Dynamics Processing effect
Loudness Meter effect: monitoring true peak, integrated loudness, platform presets (YouTube, Netflix, Spotify, Apple Podcast)
Hard Limiter (native Premiere): ISP true peak limiting at -1 dB ceiling
FIRCOMP (free third-party): sub-1ms attack compressor for peak reduction before limiter stage
Limiter Number 6 (free, Mac/PC): multi-stage limiting (peak limiter + leveling compressor + ISP protection)
Essential Sound panel: automatic loudness matching on dialog tracks
Cross Dissolve transition: smooth fade between clips
Opacity keyframe animation: fade in/out control
Scale keyframe animation: zoom effect on titles
content_ideas: Audio loudness workflow for podcast/video delivery
Title sequence animation formula (fade + zoom + offset timing)
contradictions: Fast attack times (0 ms) on dynamics processor create clean limiting but can sound 'chattery' on expansion phase; smooth attack times (26 ms) sound clean but don't block peaks effectively. No single setting handles both tasks.
weird_gold: FIRCOMP sub-1ms attack without distortion is rare in audio plugins; native Premiere dynamics processor generates artifacts at extreme settings; free third-party option outperforms stock tool
Inter-sample peak clipping (ISP) is a lossy-codec vulnerability that most creators ignore; native peak meters don't show it, Loudness Meter does
